CORRECTED from PASS. AVA Infrastructure Fund's core business activities focus on providing debt financing for infrastructure development projects across Nigeria (greenfield developments, expansion, recapitalisations, rehabilitation of mature assets). Its own stated objective is to deliver income to unit holders through debt financing, with management describing its strategy as allocating private credit. Same category as NIDF, CNIF, and MOFIREIF - a debt fund, not a property-holding trust, despite the infrastructure/real estate framing.

Revenue share from alcohol-industry clients is unconfirmed but the concentration signal is material - closer to a REIT overexposed to impermissible tenants than a comfortable pass. Needs customer-revenue breakdown before resolving.

CORRECTED from original PASS/VERIFY classification. Champion Breweries Plc is a straightforward alcohol producer - brews and markets Champion Lager Beer and other alcoholic beverages as core, majority-revenue products; Heineken International holds a majority equity stake since 2014. Same category as NB, Guinness, and International Breweries.

Identity management and payments-infrastructure group across three segments: Identity Management (biometric ID, card personalization for financial/healthcare/corporate clients via Card Centre Nigeria), Payments/Transactional Systems (switching via ChamsSwitch, ATM deployment via Chams Access, mobile money via ChamsMobile), and ICT Training - plus a 2026 pivot into AI/data-centre infrastructure via new subsidiary ChamsCorp. No banking, insurance, alcohol, or gambling exposure - this is fee-based payments rails/fintech infrastructure, not a lender. One standing caveat shared with ETRANZACT: mobile money operators sometimes earn interest on pooled customer float balances rather than passing it through - ChamsMobile's treatment of this is unconfirmed and sits at the financial-ratio layer, not a business-activity concern.

Diversified conglomerate across two segments: Industrial Raw Materials (chemicals, machinery, packaging supplied to food/pharma/manufacturing sectors) and Consumer Products (dairy via Chellarams DMK JV, frozen foods, apparel, bicycles, KFC franchise), plus real estate rental income. No alcohol, gambling, or interest-based lending found in segment breakdown - the earlier 'may include beverages' concern did not materialize. Minor open items: rental-property tenant mix and confirming no alcohol service at KFC outlets, both low-stakes.
Equipment leasing - ijara-style leasing is permissible in principle, but conventional lease financing structure needs verification.

CORRECTED - this is NOT Consolidated Hallmark Insurance as originally misidentified. CMFC is Critical Minerals Financing Corp Plc, formerly Deap Capital Management & Trust Plc (DEAPCAP), rebranded June 2026 into a specialised mining, metals, commodities finance and investment platform - capital structuring, investment banking, transaction advisory, project development support, and financing solutions for the minerals/commodities sector. No line-item CMFC revenue disclosure confirms this, but per typical revenue patterns of comparable mining/commodities financing corporations, 'financing solutions' and 'capital structuring' in this space are overwhelmingly monetized through structured debt and interest spread rather than fee-only advisory (the same pattern confirmed directly for UCAP once its lending subsidiary was examined) - treated as FAIL on that basis.

CORRECTED from original PASS classification, which mistakenly treated this as a property-holding REIT. MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF) is actually a government-backed mortgage lending vehicle, not a rental-property trust - its core business is originating fixed-rate mortgage loans to homebuyers at a stated 9.75% interest rate (well below commercial bank rates of 18-22%), plus construction financing guarantees to developers, with repayments recycled into new loans. Interest-bearing lending is the core product, not an incidental tenant-mix issue like genuine property REITs (NREIT, UPDCREIT, SFSREIT, UHOMREIT) - same category as the mortgage banks (INFINITY, LIVINGTRUST) already marked FAIL.

However, NAHCO Travel and Hospitality Limited (NHTL) now directly operates Sapphire Hotel, a 20-room in-terminal hotel at MMIA Terminal II (opened Feb 2026), with an on-site restaurant/lounge. No alcohol service confirmed either way in public disclosures - amenities described (breakfast, lunch/dinner, business office, gym, prayer area) suggest a business-transit orientation, but F&B/bar revenue at the hotel needs direct confirmation before treating as fully clean. Not comparable to Ikeja Hotel (no casino/nightclub indicated).

Own operated business (NGX Exchange, NGX RegCo, NGX RelCo) is fee-based - listing/trading fees, market data, regulation, real estate - not itself riba, comparable to how most global exchange operators are treated. Complication sits in the Strategic Investment segment: NGX Group holds equity stakes in CSCS and NASD (fine, fee-based) but also in FMDQ Securities Exchange, a market dedicated almost entirely to conventional bond/money-market/FX trading. Stake size and FMDQ's own revenue mix are unconfirmed - determines whether this is an immaterial minority holding or a taint on the parent. Genuine scholarly judgment call, not resolved by financial ratios alone.

CORRECTED from original PASS/VERIFY classification. Nigeria Infrastructure Debt Fund is explicitly a debt fund, not a property-holding trust - it makes primarily debt investments in infrastructure projects, targeting a gross return of 3.00-4.50% over comparable FGN bond yields, with 80% of assets in senior debt/securitised debt/loans to government agencies. Income to unit-holders comes from coupon and fees received from borrowers. This is interest-based lending as the core, explicit product (not incidental), same category as MOFIREIF, INFINITY, and LIVINGTRUST.
Flour milling - permissible core activity.
Microfinance bank - interest-based lending (riba).

Chapel Hill Denham Nigeria Real Estate Investment Trust - unlike other REIT-labeled NGX names on this list, NREIT is an actually certified Shariah-compliant fund, not just an inferred one: it has a named Shariah Adviser (Lotus Financial Services Limited), offer documents explicitly commit proceeds to Shariah-compliant, income-producing commercial real estate (office, retail, industrial, corporate residential), and management states a strategy of avoiding heavy reliance on debt financing - addressing the debt-ratio screen directly, not just business activity. Appears to be the only NGX REIT with actual third-party Shariah certification; the other REIT names (UHOMREIT, SFSREIT, UPDCREIT, AVAIF, CNIF) should not be assumed equivalent and still need their own tenant-mix/debt-structure check.

However, its own governing allocation rules typically invest 75% in real estate and 25% in real estate related investments such as mortgages, real estate backed securities and real estate related equities, plus a 10% cash buffer, and its own risk disclosures confirm exposure to unfavorable Interest Rate fluctuations due to the sensitivity of its financial instruments. Up to a quarter of the portfolio is structurally earmarked for interest-bearing mortgage/debt instruments - a disclosed financial-ratio concern, not an activity-level exclusion like the pure debt funds (NIDF/CNIF/MOFIREIF/AVAIF).

However, wholly owned subsidiary Tantainment Limited runs a 'live-game show' platform called 'Chances by Tantainment' (Q2 2026 launch, ~N30bn valuation, 10% stake sold to RGM Materials Solutions for N2bn). Public disclosures don't clarify whether 'Chances' involves real-money wagering/betting by viewers or is a production-funded prize/entertainment format - the name, emphasis on 'regulatory and compliance frameworks,' and 'tech-driven platform' framing warrant direct verification (terms of participation, NLRC or state gaming-authority licensing status) before resolving either way. FAIL if wagering-based; PASS likely holds if it's a skill/entertainment format with no player-side stakes.

The Initiates Plc - Nigeria's only listed environmental/waste management solutions company. Core activities: hazardous and non-hazardous waste treatment, asbestos handling, wastewater treatment, e-waste processing, thermal desorption, and industrial cleaning/decontamination services, primarily serving the Oil & Gas sector. ISO 9001:2015 and 14001:2015 certified. Expanding via majority-owned Uganda subsidiary, funded through internal cash flow (no conventional debt). No lending/insurance/alcohol/gambling exposure - a clean, regulation-driven service business.

Core business (acquiring/developing/managing/selling real estate) is genuinely permissible. However, managed by Union Homes Savings & Loans Plc, a subsidiary of Union Bank of Nigeria Plc, and the Fund Managers spread the portfolio mix across commercial and residential property investment and mortgage assets - i.e., the fund directly holds mortgage assets, not just property. Same financial-ratio concern as SFSREIT, arguably more explicit given the direct mortgage-asset holdings.
